title: Computed, not Memorized: Bit-Factorized Identifiers for Efficient Generative Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2610.17467v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Generative retrieval is known for its efficient end-to-end indexing and retrieval. In particular, numeric Document Identifiers (DocIDs) are generally more efficient because they are shorter and generally fixed-length sequences over a small vocabulary, requiring fewer decoding steps during beam search. However, they tend to generalize poorly to unseen documents and must be learned during indexing-stage training. In this paper, we propose a numeric DocID design for generative retrieval that enables better adaptation to unseen documents without retraining. Our DocID design inherits the language model's knowledge: each DocID is a sequence of tokens factorized into bits, and each token is scored as the sum of its bits. translated_title: 计算而非记忆：面向高效生成式检索的位分解标识符
translated_abstract: 生成式检索以其高效的端到端索引和检索而闻名。特别是，数字文档标识符（DocID）通常更加高效，因为它们是在小词表上更短且通常为固定长度的序列，在束搜索期间需要更少的解码步骤。然而，它们对未见过的文档泛化能力较差，必须在索引阶段的训练中学习得到。在本文中，我们提出了一种用于生成式检索的数字DocID设计，无需重新训练即可更好地适应未见过的文档。我们的DocID设计继承了语言模型的知识：每个DocID是一个被分解为比特的token序列，每个token的得分是其各比特得分之和。与现有的数字DocID不同——其token仅通过索引训练期间记忆的嵌入来承载含义——这里的每个比特都从模型的表示中获取其含义。因此，未见过的文档的DocID……
tldr: 提出了一种将DocID分解为比特进行计算而非记忆的新型数字文档标识符设计，使生成式检索无需重新训练即可更好地泛化到未见过的文档。
en_tdlr: Proposes a novel bit-factorized numeric DocID design that computes rather than memorizes token meanings, enabling generative retrieval to better generalize to unseen documents without retraining.
